sourceCitation: Catálogo Alfabético de Apellidos (1849), Archivo Histórico Nacional
lore: Governor-General Narciso Clavería y Zaldúa issues a decree standardizing native surnames. You are summoned by the Cabeza de Barangay to register your household tribute list.

choices.text: Insist on retaining your pre-colonial ancestral patronym without Christian catalog names.
choices.cause: Sentenced to hard labor in the Cavite naval arsenals for civil insubordination.
choices.trivia: The 1849 decree strictly enforced cataloged names to prevent polo labor evasion and fix tribute registers.

choices.text: Accept an assigned surname from the catalog and register your household tribute list.

sourceCitation: Gaceta de Manila (1882); Archivo de la Real Audiencia
lore: Asiatic cholera sweeps through Tondo. Spanish health authorities place armed cordons around your arrabal, forbidding movement beyond parish borders.

choices.text: Attempt to sneak across the Pasig River barricade after evening curfew.
choices.cause: Shot on sight by the Guardia Civil enforcing the sanitary cordon.
choices.trivia: During the 1882 epidemic, armed patrols strictly enforced lethal quarantine boundaries around Manila parishes.

choices.text: Boil river water, respect the curfew, and remain inside the cordoned parish boundary.

year: 1834 — Opening of the Port of Manila
sourceCitation: Real Decreto de 1834; Records of the Real Aduana
lore: Royal decree opens Manila to international commerce. Foreign merchants establish trading houses outside the Intramuros walls. A British trading clerk offers you an unvetted currency exchange.

choices.text: Conduct unauthorized coin arbitrage outside the supervision of the Real Aduana.
choices.cause: Arrested for illegal currency speculation and sentenced to penal servitude in Guam.
choices.trivia: The Royal Customs (Real Aduana) heavily regulated all bullion and foreign trade transactions under penalty of exile.

choices.text: Conduct transactions strictly in official Silver Pesos through certified brokers.

sourceCitation: Bando de Guerra del Gobernador General Blanco (Agosto 1896)
lore: Governor-General Ramón Blanco proclaims martial law over eight provinces. Guardia Civil patrols conduct warrantless searches for Katipunan membership papers.

choices.text: Keep unregistered Masonic pamphlets and handwritten cipher sheets in your wooden chest.
choices.cause: Summarily convicted of treason and executed by firing squad at Bagumbayan.
choices.trivia: Suspected subversives caught with illicit pamphlets faced immediate military tribunal and execution in 1896.

choices.text: Destroy suspicious private correspondences and ensure your Cédula Personal is stamped.
